points.description: Says classification maps data/inputs to discrete labels or categories (classes).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says classification is about categories/predicting a class without clear contrast.

points.description: Says regression maps data/inputs to continuous or real-valued outputs, so the difference is discrete vs continuous output.
points.partial_credit: Half if regression is described as predicting numbers/values but without clearly contrasting with classification.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that classification outputs discrete labels and regression outputs continuous/real values, in any wording. Give half marks for vague but related answers (e.g. 'classification sorts things, regression predicts numbers'). Error measures (misclassification count vs summed distance) are optional extras; no marks for wrong or off-topic answers.
